heading: Where to Eat in Kelowna
title: Where to Eat in Kelowna: Restaurants & Cafés | Okanagan Roam
description: Where to eat in Kelowna: dinners worth booking, Pandosy and Rutland favourites, global flavours, fish and chips, family spots, coffee and plant-based picks.
intro: Kelowna has more places to eat than any other town in the valley, and the good ones aren't all on Bernard Avenue. This guide spreads out across the city: special-occasion dinners, neighbourhood kitchens in Pandosy and Rutland, cooking from Cuba to the Philippines, old-school fish and chips, easy family meals, serious coffee and fully plant-based menus.

We've kept this list mostly to places our other Kelowna guides don't cover, so use them together. For mornings, see {page:/guides/best-brunch-kelowna|the best brunch in Kelowna}. For eating outside, try {page:/guides/best-patios-kelowna|Kelowna's best patios}. For drinks and deals, there's {page:/guides/happy-hour-kelowna|happy hour in Kelowna} and {page:/guides/cheap-eats-kelowna|cheap eats in Kelowna}, and for a night out for two, {page:/guides/date-night-kelowna|date night in Kelowna}. Some kitchens, especially winery restaurants, cut back their hours from November to April, so check each listing first.

sections.heading: Dinner worth booking
sections.lead: For a celebration, or a night when the meal is the plan.

items.name: La Bussola Restaurant
items.text: fine-dining Italian built on a slow-cooked tomato sauce. The kitchen takes dietary needs seriously and once served a gluten-free, dairy-sensitive guest real gnocchi.

items.name: Gather Restaurant
items.text: an elegant room that blends Italian and Korean cooking into one ambitious, strikingly plated menu. Order a dish that leans into both.

items.name: Okanagan Table
items.text: a farm-to-table event kitchen on Pandosy St, run by chef Rod and Audrey, with 25 years of local reputation behind it. Book one of the Signature Friday dinners or a private hosted meal.

items.name: Journey Restaurant
items.text: the winery restaurant at Azhadi Vineyards, led by Group Executive Chef Alain Leger, blending Persian heritage with classical French technique.

items.name: Home Block at CedarCreek Estate Winery
items.text: fine dining at the winery, with panoramic views of West Kelowna and a rotating menu. Ask what's on now.

sections.heading: Neighbourhood favourites
sections.lead: The places locals keep going back to, from Pandosy and the Mission to Rutland and downtown.

items.name: Mr. Lu's Kitchen
items.text: a Chinese kitchen serving regional flavour rather than a generalized version. It's open most days for lunch, and the cumin lamb is the dish to order.

items.name: Zabb Thai Restaurant
items.text: years of dependable, consistently excellent Thai cooking. For two people, the dinner-for-two preset menu is the easy order.

items.name: Bright Jenny Coffee
items.text: a neighbourhood hub for families and coffee purists, with a kids' play area, excellent latte art and a roomy, unhurried space.

items.name: Taki Japanese Grill
items.text: a longtime Rutland favourite. Order a bento box: big portions at reasonable prices.

items.name: Shambhu's Spice House Cuisine of India
items.text: the owner once walked a family through an onion- and garlic-free meal. Mention any restrictions freely.

items.name: Wasabi Ramen and Izakaya
items.text: tucked off Bernard Ave, with a quiet, devoted following. Order the okonomiyaki and one of the rich ramen broths.

sections.heading: Global flavours
sections.lead: A short tour of the world without leaving town.

items.name: Soul De Cuba Cafe
items.text: authentic Cuban on Sunset Dr that draws visitors from as far as Vancouver. Order the ropa vieja poutine and the croquettes.

items.name: Salsa & Sabor
items.text: a hole-in-the-wall in a residential area serving fresh Latin American and Colombian cooking. Get the tacos or arepas, and expect a short wait.

items.name: Jeepney Republiq
items.text: Filipino cooking in a hotel setting, with a nostalgic, homestyle menu. Order the generous pancit palabok.

items.name: Yamas Taverna
items.text: a lively Greek taverna with music keeping the meal upbeat. The roast lamb and the calamari both come in generous portions.

items.name: Bon Ga Korean Cuisine
items.text: a wholesome, family-owned kitchen. Build your order around the hot bone soup, especially on a cold day, and the spicy rice cake.

items.name: SUSHI HAYASHI
items.text: a tiny counter where you watch the chef work up close. The sushi tower and the katsu both get specific praise.

sections.heading: Seafood & steak
sections.lead: From a fish and chips shop open since 1948 to a new oyster bar.

items.name: Raw Action Oyster Co.
items.text: a buzzing new oyster bar with fresh west coast oysters, scallops and caviar. Gluten-free options are thought through, and the caviar makes it something extra special.

items.name: Shady Rest Fish & Chips
items.text: serving Kelowna since 1948, now with its fourth family of owners. Fries are cut in-house, and the halibut and cod are fresh.

items.name: Broken Anchor Cafe and Catering
items.text: a small, spotless shop where every fish and chips option is gluten-free. Regulars mention the tartar sauce, and the gluten-free pineapple fritters surprise people.

items.name: Codfather's Seafood Market
items.text: a fish market and counter in one, with halibut and chips in a light, crisp batter and whatever's fresh that day.

items.name: Derrick's Steakhouse
items.text: an upscale steakhouse with a special-occasion feel that still works with kids at the table. Book it for a family celebration.

sections.heading: Casual & family
sections.lead: Easy meals where nobody minds a bit of noise.

items.name: Antico Pizza Napoletana
items.text: reviewers say it feels like eating pizza in Italy, with the char and chew of a proper Neapolitan crust. Staff are patient with families.

items.name: BNA Burger
items.text: order at the counter, get a proper smash burger and find a seat on the patio. No reservation, no fuss.

items.name: THYME at Ellison Lake
items.text: a friendly, reasonably priced family restaurant near Ellison Lake Park. Order the flatbread and a homemade cinnamon bun.

items.name: Cecil's Perogy Palace
items.text: fresh, generously portioned perogies for years, consistent rather than trendy. Comfort food that tastes like home cooking.

items.name: Convair Cafe
items.text: an aviation-themed cafe near the airport hangars, with airplane seating and a highchair for babies. The pesto turkey croissant is the beloved order.

sections.heading: Coffee & bakeries
sections.lead: For your morning cup, or something to carry out the door.

items.name: Anarchy Coffee Roasters
items.text: locals fiercely defend it as the home of Kelowna's best cappuccino. Art-covered walls, a worn-in couch and a little free library.

items.name: Twin Sparks Coffee Roasters
items.text: a hole-in-the-wall roastery with a creative streak. Order the torched banana latte.

items.name: Polene Bakery & Bistro
items.text: a tiny Bernard Ave counter that reviewers call the best sandwich shop in Kelowna, built on excellent house-made bread.

items.name: Cake Otaku
items.text: a new Japanese bakery whose curry buns and mochi sell out within hours of opening. Arrive right at open.

items.name: Sprout Bread
items.text: the bakery-cafe locals head to after a hike or ride, for excellent coffee and fresh-baked pastries. Expect a lineup.

sections.heading: Plant-based
sections.lead: Full vegan menus that non-vegans enjoy too.

items.name: Frankie We Salute You!
items.text: vegan fine dining in an industrial-feel room, with family-sourced and local Okanagan produce, gluten-free items and a thoughtful lapsang mocktail.

items.name: Naked Cafe
items.text: a dedicated vegan cafe and a Kelowna favourite for years. Its reputation rests on the sushi bowls and the Japanese curry.

items.name: Zen's Plant-Based Cuisine
items.text: a newly opened, entirely vegan restaurant. Every meal starts with a complimentary tea or soy-milk coffee; order the cashew Alfredo or a mushroom bowl.

items.name: Nature's Table at Summerhill
items.text: the restaurant at Summerhill Pyramid Winery, with a thoughtful vegan and vegetarian menu. Pair it with the certified organic wine.
